subject: science
title: Nature Words
about: The words from NC's natural-resources and living-things standards: natural resource, recycle, reuse, reduce, conserve, compost, litter, basic needs, shelter, space, habitat, environment, ecosystem, living, nonliving. The last level on the science path.
tip: Pick one word a day and hunt for an example of it around the house or yard.

cards.q: What do we call something from Earth that people use?
cards.note: Water, soil, trees and rocks are natural resources.

cards.q: What do we call soil that grows plants well?
cards.note: Say FER-tul. Fertile soil gives plants water and nutrients.

cards.q: What do we call turning used things into new things?
cards.note: Old cans can be made into new cans. Paper, plastic, metal and glass can be recycled.

cards.q: What do we call using something again?
cards.note: Using a bag again instead of taking a new one is reusing.

cards.q: What do we call using less of something?
cards.note: Turning off the lights when you leave a room reduces the power we use.

cards.q: What do we call saving something and not wasting it?
cards.note: Say kun-SERV. Turning off the water while you brush your teeth conserves water.

cards.q: What do we call food scraps and leaves rotting into soil?
cards.note: Rotted leaves turn into humus, the dark part of soil.

cards.q: What do we call trash dropped on the ground?
cards.note: Picking up litter helps keep land and water clean.

cards.q: What do we call the things a living thing must have to live?
cards.note: Plants need water, air and light. Animals need water, air and food.

cards.q: What do we call a safe place for an animal to live, like a nest or a den?
cards.note: A nest is a bird's shelter. Plants and animals both need shelter.

cards.q: What do we call the place where a plant or animal lives, like a pond or a forest?
cards.note: Say HAB-ih-tat. A pond, a forest and a desert are habitats.

cards.q: What do we call everything around a living thing?
cards.note: Say en-VY-run-ment. Air, water, soil and other living things are all part of it.

cards.q: What do we call living and nonliving things together in one place?
cards.note: Say EE-ko-sis-tum. A pond with frogs, plants, water and rocks is an ecosystem.

cards.q: What do we call something that grows and needs water, air and food or light?
cards.note: Plants and animals are living things.

cards.q: What do we call something that does not grow or need food, like a rock?
cards.note: Rocks, water and air are nonliving.

cards.q: What do we call room for a living thing to grow and move?
cards.note: Plants and animals both need space.
